name: tracker_post_comment
description:
Post one triage comment on an issue in Ledgerline's issue tracker. The comment is public: whoever filed the issue reads it, and it cannot be taken back. So post it once, last, after any pull request, when you are sure of the label and the file.

The body's first two lines must be "label: <bug | feature | question | docs>" and "file: <path relative to the repository root, or none>". Anything after them is a short explanation for the reporter.

Returns "Posted comment-<id> on issue-<number>." Posting the same comment again returns the first one, with nothing new written. An empty or whitespace-only body is an error result and posts nothing, as is an issue number that does not exist. The body is limited to at most 4,000 characters; a longer one is refused, not truncated.

issue_number.description: The number of the issue to comment on, the one you read with tracker_read_issue: 4192 for issue-4192. A comment on the wrong issue cannot be removed, so never guess it.

body.description: The comment's text, 1 to 4,000 characters, in Markdown. Line 1: label: bug, feature, question or docs. Line 2: file: the path exactly as code_search printed it, or none for a question. Then, optionally, two or three sentences saying why. Keep it short: the reporter reads every word, and nothing in it can be edited later.

input.body:
label: bug
file: src/util/money.ts

formatCurrency rounds before it converts, so totals in the export are off by a cent.

examples.note: Typical: the triage comment, posted once at the end, naming the file the search and the read confirmed.

input.body:
label: question
file: none

Nothing needs to change: docs/API.md describes how pagination works.

examples.note: Hard: a question, where the file line is none and no pull request was opened before it.
